messages:
maya: Heads-up — since ~08:10 UTC eu-west-2 / eu2 inference tail latencies are spiking for small requests. 95p token latency up ~3x, p99 worse. GPU util is lumpy (one host hitting 98% while neighbours idle). Looks like a large synchronous batched job from tenant acme-ai is hammering NVLink/PCIe and saturating NIC queues.

infra-bot: ALERT: gpu-cluster-eu2 host-group 'rt-pool' high gpu_util(98%), net_tx_drop rising. Incident ID: #INC-20240315-1723

tom: Oof. Can we immediately isolate that tenant traffic? Route them to a different pool or throttle?

maya: I tried a soft quota (rate-limit) but their job is single-process huge batches, so it just filled the device. Quota didn't preempt the job. Snapshot of metrics:
```
host: gpu-node-12.eu2
GPU util: 98%
NVLink bw util: 92%
pcie saturated: yes
net tx qlen drops: 120/sec
inference p95: 420ms -> baseline 140ms
```

joseph: Two quick options: 1) MIG slice that GPU into isolated partitions for inference vs train (works if model fits), 2) network + kernel level shaping so training can't hog NIC/PCIe buffers. MIG requires model compatibility and a job restart.

li: MIG is ideal for long-term but requires scheduling changes and tenant consent. Dedicated reservation for acme-ai would avoid noisy neighbor entirely but will add committed cost. Rough back-of-envelope: reserving 4x p4d equivalent in eu2 ~ $22k/mo.

ari: Routing idea: prefer dpool if tenant.labels.enterprise == true OR tenant.active_job_type == "batch_train" -> route to dedicated or cpu-backend fallback. Example policy snippet:
```
{
  "policy": [
    {"if": "tenant.metadata.reserved_pool == true", "route": "dedicated"},
    {"if": "gpu_capacity.available < 2 && tenant.tier != 'enterprise'", "route": "fallback-cpu"}
  ]
}
```

tom: Immediate mitigation plan I can run now: apply a qdisc shaper on host to limit acme-ai's pod network egress and attach cgroup net_cls so only that container gets shaped. That should relieve NIC and driver buffers. I'll also add a kube taint + toleration to evict new heavy batches from rt-pool.

maya: Please do. We need quick relief and then talk options with ACME. CS is reaching out.

tom: Running command now (dry-run then apply):
```
# mark container cgroup
cgclassify -g net_cls:/tenants/acme-ai <pid>
# create tbf qdisc on eth0
tc qdisc add dev eth0 root handle 1: htb default 30
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1: classid 1:1 htb rate 10gbit ceil 10gbit
tc class add dev eth0 parent 1:1 classid 1:10 htb rate 20gbit ceil 20gbit
tc filter add dev eth0 parent 1:0 protocol ip prio 1 handle 0x100 fw flowid 1:10
```

deploy-bot: ACTION: running playbook infra/qos/apply for host gpu-node-12 (dry-run -> apply).

tom: Applied on node gpu-node-12 and sibling hosts in that rack.

deploy-bot: SUCCESS: tc qdisc added on gpu-node-12, gpu-node-13, gpu-node-14. Change set id: cs-20240315-87

tom: Observed latency returning toward baseline within ~3m after shaping. p95 back to ~150ms, p99 still a bit high while KV caches warm.

maya: ACME has acknowledged and agreed to pause the large job for now. They asked for dedicated capacity to avoid future disruptions.

joseph: Follow-ups we should do: 1) quick runbook for NIC/PCIe qdisc mitigation (ops playbook), 2) schedule MIG tests for common model sizes (S, M, L) to see viability, 3) routing policy to fail over to CPU-backed or dedicated pools automatically when we detect IO saturation.

li: I'll draft cost/contract options for dedicated reservations and a temporary discount for ACME to move. + run a 1-week forecast of utilization impact if they move to dedicated.

ari: I'll add a small policy change in the router to prefer dedicated for tenants flagged as "high-isolation" and add a safety cutoff: if more than 2 hosts in pool exceed 80% nvlink_util -> expand route to fallback-cpu. I'll open a PR for review.

maya: Nice. Action items (owners):
- tom: document and deploy tc-qdisc runbook, add kube taint pattern (today)
- joseph: MIG compatibility matrix + test runs (this week)
- li: cost/contract options + forecast (EOD tomorrow)
- ari: router policy PR + canary (this sprint)
- maya: coordinate with ACME and confirm dedicated reservation request (today)

maya: Thanks everyone — leaving monitoring on this thread. If latency regresses, I'll ping paging. :thumbsup:

tom: +1

joseph: :+1:

infra-bot: RESOLVE: Incident #INC-20240315-1723 mitigated by qos shaping and tenant pause. Monitoring for 2h.
